newsitem.title: EGYPT: SQUASH-JANSHER THREATENS TO BOYCOTT PAKISTAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER THREATENS TO BOYCOTT PAKISTAN OPEN.

text.p: Squash world champion Jansher Khan said on Monday he would boycott the Pakistan Open in Karachi in August unless the Pakistani federation attracted more publicity about squash events played in the country.

Jansher told reporters in Cairo, where he is competing in the al-Ahram International Squash Championship, that television coverage was the best way to popularise the game in Pakistan, especially among young people.

He said the sport was gaining ground in Egypt because of the media coverage of teenaged local hero Ahmed Barada, now ranked fifth in the world and one of the semifinalists in the $140,000 al-Ahram championship.

"This is the sort of attention I would like a chance to discuss with (Pakistani) Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. Egyptian squash has taken off because the government and the television companies follow Barada's progress at home and abroad," he said.

"I am the best in the world. Before I finish I will establish records no other player will ever equal. Pakistan must take advantage of that and until the (Pakistan Squash) Federation takes action in the direction I will not play in another Pakistan Open," he added.
"When I won the World Open title in Karachi, only the final was shown on Pakistan television and that went out at 2.30 in the afternoon, when everyone was working or sleeping," he said.
Jansher said he wrote to the president of the Pakistan federation, Air Chief Marshal Abbas Khatak, four months ago suggesting a meeting with Nawaz Sharif but had heard nothing in response.

"When I ring Abbas Khatak now, I am just told he is too busy to talk to me. We are all busy... But if we do not do something now about promoting our success in squash, Pakistan will lose the leadership of the game," he said.
